0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards In-titution on 28 November 1986, after the draft finalized by the Animal Feeds Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 0.2 Meat meal is one of the important protein supplements USE"d in livestock feed This material, besides serving as a protein supplement, also provides mine! als, particularly, calcium and phosphorus to the livestock. Mr at meal is a by-product obtained from the dead animal rendering pl.mt� In order to exercise proper quality control during their production, it is considere-d necessary to have standards for this product. It is expected that this standard would also assist the consumer to procure meat meal of a known quality. 0.3 This standard was first published in 1969. In this revision moisture content has been reduced. Fur t her, reference has been given to IS : 7874 (Part I ).1975'" and IS: 7874 (Part 2 )-197:'t for adopting uniform test methods. Title of t his standard has also been revised. 0.4 In the pi epar ation meat meal the carcasses of dead animals, which mayor may not have been debonetl, are first boiled in opf'n cauldrons or in closed vessels, and rheu dried in steam jacketed vessels. The dried material is then pulverized.

I. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements, and methods of sampling and test for meat meal meant for use as a livestock feed ingredient.

2. REQ,UIREMENTS
2.1 General - Meat meal shall be coarse, deep brawn coloured powdery material. The material shall be free from adulterants and visible insect and fungal infestation. Meat meal shall be free from odour indicative of rancidity or any other objectionable odour but shall possess an odour characteristic of these products. 2.2 Freedom from Pathogens - Meat meal shall be free from spores of Bacillus anthracts, Clostridium sp and Salmonella when tested according to the method prescribed in 4~ 5, 6 and 9 of IS : 7874 ( Part 3 )-1975"'.
2.3 Meat meal shall also conform 10 the requirements prescribed in Table 1.

3. PACKING AND MARKING
3.1 Packing - The materia) shall be packed in moisture-proof bags or
HDPE bags or in any other suitable container suhject to the agreement between the purchaser and the vendor. The container shall be sound, clean and free from casual agents of infectious diseases and parasites. The mouth of each bag shall either he machine-stitched or rolled over and hand-stitched with SfJ oog twine.

3.2 Marking - F ach
information: a) b) c) d)

bag shall

be

rna, ked

with the

following

Name of the material; Name of the manufacturer; Net mass in kg, when packed; anti Batch or rode number.

3.2.1 The bags may also be marked with the Standard Mark.
NOTE - The USI' of the Standarrl Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau or Indian Standards ALt, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder, The Standard Mark on product- covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that thr-y have heen produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a wpll defined system of inspect ion, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised hy HIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuous I v checked by B IS for conform ity to that standard as a further safeguard. Detarls of conditions under which a licence for the usc of the Standard Mark mav be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

4. SAMPLING
4.1 Representative samples of the material for test shall be drawn
according to the method prescribed in Appendix C of 15 : 2052-197<)�.

5.1 The tests shall be carried out as referred to in col 4 and 5 of Table 1 and 2.2.
